title: Cryptographic consent attestation
description: Records that a wallet has cryptographically attested to an off-chain legal document identified by its keccak256 content hash. The pattern is: off-chain document semantics, on-chain anchor for shared reference integrity. Per PROTOCOL_EXTENSION_DOCTRINE.md §'Decision Rule', the protocol needs the (consenter, documentHash, documentVersion, documentTitle) tuple to preserve shared reference integrity across counterparties (participant, operator, future auditors, possibly arbitrators, possibly courts) over time. Consenter address is recoverable from the EIP-712 signature on the AttestationCoordinator call (visible in the Attestation event) — not stored in content. Block timestamp captures when. Append-only: revocation is a separate off-chain process, not a content mutation; future revisions require figaro-consent-v2.

fields.name: documentHash
fields.description: keccak256 of the canonical legal document text. The 32-byte content anchor; the document itself lives off-chain (e.g., served as a PDF, pinned to IPFS, or distributed alongside the receipt). Any byte-level change to the document produces a different hash and therefore a different attestation.

fields.name: documentVersion
fields.description: Semver-style version identifier (e.g., '1.0.0', '2025-04-29'). Bounded to 32 chars to prevent griefing via unbounded calldata. Pairs with documentHash so a reader can disambiguate two documents that share a title but differ in content.

fields.name: documentTitle
fields.description: Human-readable document name (e.g., 'Figaro Beta Informed Consent Agreement', 'Privacy Policy'). Bounded to 200 chars. Provides a label for off-chain display and dispute reference; the documentHash is the binding identifier.
